name: Sanxingdui and Ancient Shu
desc: An unknown kingdom of the Sichuan basin whose sacrificial pits held bronze heads with bulging eyes, a standing bronze figure taller than a man, bronze trees with birds on their branches, gold masks and hundreds of elephant tusks, unlike anything else in ancient China.
source: The sacrificial pits of Sanxingdui, found in 1986 and more since 2020; the Jinsha site in Chengdu; the Chronicles of Huayang

devout: wore the great mask with the long eyes at the spring rite
cautious: beat a lump of gold into a mask as thin as a leaf
gluttonous: caught a fish as long as my arm with a cormorant

inventions.name: Bronze Masks
inventions.source: Bronze heads and masks from Sanxingdui, some with cylindrical eyes jutting out, the largest over 1.3 m wide
inventions.desc: Great bronze faces with eyes that stare out of their heads, to let the spirits see: rites bring 15% more devotion, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs Bronze Metallurgy, and long rites.

inventions.name: Bronze Sacred Tree
inventions.source: Bronze tree no. 1 from Sanxingdui, nearly 4 m tall, with nine birds on its branches and a dragon climbing down the trunk
inventions.desc: A tree of bronze reaching from earth to sky, with sun-birds on its branches: +3 mood, rites bring 5% more devotion.
inventions.hint: Needs Bronze Metallurgy and the Bronze & Mythic Era.

inventions.name: Gold Leaf
inventions.source: Gold masks from Sanxingdui and the gold foil 'Sun and Immortal Birds' from Jinsha, now the emblem of Chinese cultural heritage
inventions.desc: Gold beaten as thin as paper and cut into masks and circles of flying birds: +2 mood, rites bring 5% more devotion.

inventions.name: Bieling's Channels
inventions.source: Chronicles of Huayang: Bieling cut through the mountains to drain the flood of the Chengdu plain; Li Bing's Dujiangyan (256 BCE) later did the same
inventions.desc: Channels cut to spread the mountain river across the plain instead of letting it flood: farm plots yield 25% more.
inventions.hint: Needs farming and Polished Stone Tools.

foods.name: Fish with Sichuan Pepper
foods.source: Sichuan pepper (huajiao) is native to the region and was used in China from very early times
foods.desc: River fish cooked with the numbing red pepper of the hills: +3 mood, hunger grows 5% slower.

foods.name: Rice of the Plain
foods.desc: Rice from the wet fields of the plain, boiled in pots: hunger grows 10% slower.

finds.name: Sichuan Pepper Bushes
finds.desc: Thorny shrubs with red husks that make the tongue tingle.

finds.name: River Gold
finds.desc: Glittering grains in the river sand below the mountains.

people.name: Mu Ya
people.desc: When he wears the mask, he says, he can see beyond the mountains.
memory: led the procession of masks around the bronze tree

people.name: Yu Fu
people.desc: His birds bring him fish from the bottom of the river.
memory: trained a cormorant that brought back seven fish in an hour

people.name: Cancong
people.source: Chronicles of Huayang; Li Bai, 'Hard is the Road to Shu'
people.desc: The first king of Shu, whose eyes stood out from his head; he taught the people to raise silkworms.

people.name: Yufu
people.desc: An early king of Shu whose name means 'fish-hawk', remembered for his hunting and fishing, and said to have become an immortal.

people.name: Luo Zhang
people.source: Jade yazhang blades of the Erlitou type were found at Sanxingdui, showing contact with the Central Plains
people.text: a traveller who has come over the mountain roads from the north with a jade blade, the sign of the kings of the Central Plains.
memory: crossed the plank roads clinging to the cliffs above the Jialing
people.desc: A traveller from the Central Plains, of the kind who brought jade blades to Shu.

people.name: Duyu
people.label: Duyu, the Cuckoo King
people.desc: He teaches the people to farm, and becomes a cuckoo. Foraging 7, Lore 5.

people.name: Bieling
people.label: Bieling, who Drained the Flood
people.desc: A dead man who floated upstream and came to life to tame the waters. Crafting 8.

people.name: The Standing One
people.label: The Standing One, Great Shaman of Shu
people.desc: Taller than any man, his empty hands once held something no one remembers. Lore 7, Combat 6.

events.title: Break and Bury the Treasures
events.source: The Sanxingdui pits held bronzes, jades and tusks that had been deliberately broken, burned and buried; why is still unknown
events.text: The priests say the old masks and vessels have served their time. They must be broken, burned and buried in a pit with the tusks, and new ones made.

options.label: Break and bury them

do.feat: Buried the old treasures in the sacred pit

options.result: The pit is filled and covered. Three thousand years later, someone will dig it up and the world will gasp.

options.label: Keep them
options.result: The old masks stay on their stands. The priests are uneasy.

events.title: The Earthquake Moves the River
events.source: One theory holds that an earthquake around 1100 BCE dammed the Min and moved the river away from Sanxingdui, and the capital moved to Jinsha
events.text: The ground shook, a hillside fell into the river, and now the water runs far from the town. The elders argue about whether to follow it.

options.label: Move to the new river
options.result: A new town is built by the river, on the site the people call 'the Golden Sand'.

options.label: Dig a channel to the old town
options.result: The water comes back to the old walls.

events.title: Tusks from the Southern Forests
events.source: Over a thousand elephant tusks were found at Sanxingdui and Jinsha; wild elephants then lived in the region
events.text: Hunters come back from the southern forests with the tusks of elephants. The priests want them for the great rites; the carvers want them for combs and bracelets.

options.label: Give them to the gods
options.result: The tusks are laid around the altar.

options.label: Carve them
options.result: Combs and bracelets of white ivory appear on every wrist.

tales.name: The King Whose Eyes Stood Out
tales.text: The first king of our land had eyes that stood out from his face like two horns, so that he could see far over the mountains. He saw the silkworms on the mulberry trees and taught the people to raise them, and wherever he went they built shrines.

tales.name: The Fusang Tree and the Ten Suns
tales.source: Shanhai Jing, Classic of the Regions Beyond the Eastern Seas
tales.text: Far in the east grows the Fusang tree, where the ten suns, each carried by a bird, bathe in the hot spring. Nine rest in the lower branches while one rises to cross the sky. The bronze tree in our temple is that tree, and its birds are those suns.

tales.name: The King Who Became a Cuckoo
tales.source: Chronicles of Huayang; Li Shangyin, 'The Brocade Zither'
tales.text: King Duyu taught the people to farm, then gave his throne to the man who had drained the flood, and went into the mountains. When he died, his spirit became a cuckoo that cries every spring, 'Time to sow! Time to sow!' until blood comes from its throat, and the azaleas are red with it.

tales.name: The Four Sun-Birds
tales.source: The gold foil disc of Jinsha, c. 1000 BCE
tales.text: On the great day of the sun, the priests hold up a circle of gold leaf, thin as a petal: a sun with twelve flaming rays, and four birds flying round it, one for each season. The light shines through it onto the faces of the people.
tales.moral: the year turns like birds round the sun
